basic_identification.full_title: Cold Rolled Non-Oriented Electrical Steel Sheet and Strip - Semi-Processed Type - Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard covers the requirements of cold rolled non-oriented electrical steel sheet and strip in a semi-processed condition, designed for the construction of magnetic circuits. It applies to sheet and strip of nominal thicknesses of 0.50 mm and 0.65 mm.

amendment_slips.description: Modifies Table 2 and Table 3 column headers on Page 3 and Page 4, substituting the words 'Minimum Magnetic Polarization' for 'Maximum Magnetic Polarization'.

Substitutes Clause 11 on Page 5 regarding surface conditions to permit minor defects (such as scratches, blisters, and cracks) if they fall within thickness tolerances and do not interfere with processing. It also changes a value under Clause 11.1 from '1.5' to '1.2'.
Modifies the definition of 'Narrow Strip' in Clause 3.6.2 to mean 'Cold rolled strip of width normally less than 600 mm.'

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Certification under the BIS Standard Mark scheme is permissive (voluntary) according to the text of the specification. While finished semi-processed sheets do not have a mandatory marking requirement written in the text, the standard establishes rigorous post-delivery quality evaluation annealing, mechanical inspection, and anti-corrosive packaging certifications.

requirements.detail: The material conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (now 2016), and marked with the Standard Mark.

Because the material is delivered in a semi-processed state, the purchaser is responsible for carrying out the final annealing heat treatment. To verify compliance of magnetic properties (core loss and polarization), test strips must be subjected to a reference heat treatment in a decarburizing atmosphere (retaining 20% hydrogen and 80% nitrogen) at specified temperatures (790 °C or 840 °C) for 2 hours.
Unless otherwise specified, the sheets or strips must be securely packed in metal-protected containers lined with water-proof material to prevent rusting or physical damage during transit.
Each delivered coil or packet of cut length must be legibly marked with the manufacturer's name/trade-mark, grade designation, dimensions (thickness, width, and sheet length), and total weight.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15391:2003 specifies the standard requirements for cold-rolled, non-oriented electrical steel sheets and strips supplied in a semi-processed state for manufacturing magnetic circuits (such as cores in rotating machines). Unlike fully processed steels, semi-processed steel requires final processing by the buyer. Therefore, the most critical design detail is ensuring the purchaser's final heat treatment matches the standard reference decarburizing anneal (heating up to 840 °C depending on the grade) to achieve compliant magnetic polarization and low specific total loss. Additionally, materials must be securely delivered in metal containers with water-proof linings to guarantee rust prevention during transit.
